metadata.title: 1-D Biot consolidation of a laterally confined, singly drained column (OGS staggered-scheme consolidation benchmark)

source.journal: OpenGeoSys 6.5.7 documentation, Benchmarks / Hydro-Mechanics; analytical solution after Murad & Loula (1992) and Korsawe et al. (2006)

metadata.validation_method: closed-form series solution (Terzaghi/Biot 1-D consolidation), plus the published OGS staggered/monolithic results at t = 10 s
metadata.validation_target: Pore-pressure history at x_D = 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.5 / 0.8, top settlement history, and the pore-pressure depth profile at t = 10 s
metadata.notes: Source of every value: https://www.opengeosys.org/6.5.7/docs/benchmarks/hydro-mechanics/consolidationbenchmark/ and the project file Tests/Data/HydroMechanics/StaggeredScheme/ConsolidationBenchmark/consolidation_benchmark.prj (E, nu, k, eta, sigma_0, biot=1, porosity=0, t_end=10 s, dt=0.5 s). Domain extent read from the accompanying mesh hm_tri_q.vtu: x in [0, 0.1], y in [-1, 0], i.e. H = 1 m deep, 0.1 m wide. In the paper's notation the depth coordinate is called x and runs from the drained top (x=0) to the sealed base (x=H); here it is -y. DISCRETISATION DIFFERENCES vs OGS, both forced by this backend: (1) OGS uses quadratic (order 2) displacement with linear pressure -- an inf-sup stable Taylor-Hood pair -- whereas upquad11 is EQUAL-ORDER linear u/p, which does not satisfy inf-sup; with dt = 0.5 s the drained boundary layer is only ~2 elements deep, so CHECK THE PRESSURE PROFILE NEAR y = 0 FOR CHECKERBOARDING before accepting the result, and refine dt/mesh if it appears. (2) OGS meshes quadratic triangles; this backend needs quads for u-p, so the mesh is recombined -- verify the console reports a pure quad mesh (see the recombine trap). (3) OGS solves the coupled system with a staggered fixed-stress split, this backend monolithically; both target the same converged solution, so this is not a modelling difference. Zero liquid storage (porosity 0, incompressible fluid) is entered as storage = 0 exactly, matching the analytical assumption. Gravity/body force is omitted in the benchmark and is not in this backend's mass balance either, so the two agree by construction.

entities._comment: PAPER_VALUE: bounding box of hm_tri_q.vtu, x in [0,0.1] m, y in [-1,0] m. Column height H = 1 m; the width is immaterial (the solution is 1-D) but is kept identical to the benchmark mesh.

physical_groups.name: column_domain
physical_groups._comment: no boolean operations are used, so entity_ids is valid here

physical_groups.name: top
physical_groups._comment: PAPER_VALUE: y = 0, the loaded and free-draining face (geometry_top.vtu)

physical_groups.name: bottom
physical_groups._comment: PAPER_VALUE: y = -H, rigid and impermeable base (geometry_bottom.vtu). It carries a uy Dirichlet but deliberately NO pore-pressure BC -- no BC = zero flux = the impervious condition dp/dn = 0.

physical_groups.name: left
physical_groups._comment: PAPER_VALUE: x = 0, rigid impermeable wall (geometry_left.vtu); ux = 0 only, uy free

physical_groups.name: right
physical_groups._comment: PAPER_VALUE: x = 0.1, rigid impermeable wall (geometry_right.vtu); ux = 0 only, uy free

points.name: probe_xD0p1
points._comment: x_D = depth/H = 0.1; x = 0.04 and y = -0.1 are multiples of element_size so they should land on nodes -- CHECK THE RUN LOG for 'Point ... away from closest node' warnings

points.name: probe_top
points._comment: settlement probe on the loaded surface

mesh._comment_recombine: REQUIRED: upquad11 is the only u-p element on this backend, so the mesh must be quads. No 'refinement' entry is used on purpose -- grading plus recombination can leave stray triangles, whose nodes are then dropped and the matrix goes singular.
mesh._comment_size: ASSUMED (matched to the benchmark): OGS uses 412 triangles over the 0.1 m^2 face, i.e. h ~ 0.022 m. 0.02 m gives 5 x 50 = 250 quads. Resolution check: the drained boundary layer after the first step is sqrt(c*dt) = sqrt(3.333e-3*0.5) = 0.041 m ~ 2 elements, and at t_end sqrt(c*10) = 0.183 m ~ 9 elements.

hydro_mechanical._comment: MONOLITHIC: displacement and pore_pressure are solved together in one tangent, so no source_field/target_field. OGS runs the same problem with a staggered fixed-stress split; the converged solution is the same.

displacement._comment_E: PAPER_VALUE: Young's modulus 3e4 Pa (parameter table / <parameter> E in the prj)
displacement._comment_rho: PAPER_VALUE-by-permission: the benchmark omits the body force and states the densities may be arbitrary non-zero values (prj: solid density 0, fluid density 1000). Density enters nothing in this quasi-static, gravity-free run.
displacement._comment_plane_state: Plane strain (the default) is REQUIRED here and is also the physically correct state: eps_zz = 0 makes the confined modulus lambda+2G = 33333.33 Pa, which is exactly what the analytical solution uses. plane_stress/thickness are rejected on a hydro_mechanical material anyway; out-of-plane depth is fixed at 1 m.

pore_pressure._comment_perm: PAPER_VALUE: permeability 1e-10 m^2 and viscosity 1e-3 Pa.s. Given by the named route so the pipeline forms the mobility itself: k/mu = 1e-7 m^2/(Pa.s). Do NOT paste 1e-10 into 'mobility'.
pore_pressure._comment_storage: PAPER_VALUE: the benchmark assumes ZERO liquid storage (porosity 0, incompressible fluid), so 1/Q = 0 exactly. The porosity+fluid_bulk_modulus route cannot express this (porosity must be > 0), hence the direct storage route. Pressure change is then driven purely by the strain rate, as the page states.
pore_pressure._comment_sanity: Consolidation coefficient c = (lambda+2G)*k/eta = 33333.33 * 1e-7 = 3.3333e-3 m^2/s, so t_D = c*t/H^2 = 3.3333e-3*t and t_end = 10 s is only t_D = 0.033 -- an EARLY-time problem: at t_end the base is still essentially undrained (p = 998 Pa at x_D = 0.8) and only the top ~0.18 m has drained.

initial_conditions._comment: PAPER_VALUE: sigma = p = 0 at t = 0 (pressure_ic in the prj). The run is driven from this consistent zero state by the surface load, which is the admissible way to start a poroelastic problem.

boundary_conditions._comment: PAPER_VALUE: sigma_0 = -1000 Pa applied on the top face (prj: Neumann, component 1, load = -1e3). A traction DENSITY in Pa, integrated over the face -- mesh-independent, and NOT to be hand-integrated into a point_load. No time_function: the benchmark loads instantaneously at t = 0 and holds, which is what the default step behaviour gives.
PAPER_VALUE: p = 0 on the drained face. A Dirichlet is right here (unlike a drying surface): 'free to drain' at atmospheric pressure means the excess pore pressure IS zero there by definition.
PAPER_VALUE: u = 0 on the rigid base. Only the NORMAL component is fixed, as on a symmetry/roller plane -- fixing ux too would over-constrain.
PAPER_VALUE: rigid lateral wall; normal component only, so the column is laterally confined (uniaxial strain) as the analytical solution assumes.

_comment_boundary_conditions: DELIBERATELY ABSENT: no pore_pressure BC on 'bottom', 'left' or 'right'. The walls are impermeable, and on this backend no BC = zero flux, which is exactly dp/dn = 0. Never write a zero-value Neumann for this.

time_stepping._comment: PAPER_VALUE: t_end = 10 s with 20 fixed steps of dt = 0.5 s (prj FixedTimeStepping; the page notes dt = 0.5 s already tracks the analytical curves). Kept uniform to reproduce the published comparison rather than log-refining the early transient. If the pressure field checkerboards near the drained face, halve dt AND the element size together -- for equal-order u/p the undrained limit is approached by SMALL dt on a COARSE mesh, so refining dt alone makes it worse.

queries.label: Dimensionless time t_D = c t / H^2
Dimensionless settlement u_D = u (lambda+2G)/(p0 H)
queries._comment: u_D -> 1 as t_D -> inf; at t_D = 0.0333 the analytical value is 0.2060 (uy = -6.180e-3 m).

queries.label: Pore pressure over depth at t = 10 s
queries._comment_endpoints: line_profile endpoints take EXACTLY the mesh dimension (2 here), NOT the 3-value geometry convention: they sample the field directly instead of snapping to a node, so a padded z is rejected. A 3rd value raised every step and ALSO produced a bogus 'never fired: at_time is outside the simulated window' warning, because a raising query leaves its id absent and the at_time warner does not verify its own claim.

queries.label: sigma_yy at x_D = 0.5 [Pa]
queries._comment: DIAGNOSTIC, not a validation curve: whether the Biot material reports the EFFECTIVE or the TOTAL stress is not documented here. Check it against the two knowns before using it -- total sigma_yy = -1000 Pa at all times and all depths, whereas the effective stress starts at 0 and relaxes to -1000 Pa. The analytical effective stress is in reference/analytical_profiles_t10s.csv (sigma_eff_yy_Pa = -1000 + p).

plots.name: pressure_profile_t10s
plots.title: Pore-pressure profile over depth at t = 10 s

curves.label: FEM, t = 10 s
curves._comment: axis is needed HERE as well as on the query: the query's own 'axis' only picks the placement axis for a SCALAR endpoint and is inert when start/end are points, and it is never carried into SpatialQueryResult. The plotter reads curve_cfg['axis'] (plotter/curves.py) and defaults to 0 - which plots the constant x of a vertical profile line and draws the FEM curve as a single vertical stripe.

plots._comment: The whole comparison lives in the top ~0.2 m; if the curves are unreadable, set xlim [-0.3, 0.0].

results._comment_reference_curves: NOT digitised from a figure -- evaluated from the closed-form series printed on the benchmark page (see reference/make_reference.py, 4000 terms). Sign/axis conventions: the paper's depth coordinate x_D = -y/H, so these files are written against the MESH coordinate y in [-1, 0] m; pressure in Pa, compression positive (both the paper and this backend); uy negative = settlement. The page prints the u_D series coefficient as 2/M, which fails the t=0 check (u must vanish everywhere in the undrained zero-storage limit); 2/M^2 is used instead.
